docs.title: From no dividend to 3.5% yield: This PSU bank’s profit-led comeback is not over
docs.text: Welcome to the latest edition of Dividend Hunter. In recent weeks, we have analysed companies where strong cash flows could translate into consistent dividends. In our previous edition, we covered a public sector undertaking (PSU) Bank that delivered a 3.7% dividend yield. This week, in our 'Dividend Hunter' series, we are discussing another fast-growing and India’s sixth-largest government-owned bank with a market capitalisation of ₹1,08,476 crore as of October 9, 2026. In FY26, the bank recorded a global business of ₹28.06 lakh crore alongside a record annual net profit of ₹19,187.0 crore. Notably, the bank's revenue grew at a 12% CAGR over the past five years, while net profit rose at a much faster CAGR of 44%. Strong asset quality also supported the company’s profitability. Gross and Net Non-Performing Asset (NPA) levels were 1.84% and 0.43%, respectively. The bank also delivered a 19.6% return on equity (ROE) and 1.1% return on assets (ROA). The bank maintains a clear policy to deliver periodic cash returns to its shareholders. For FY26, the Board recommended a dividend of ₹4.20 per share. Effectively, this public sector bank continues to balance capital appreciation with shareholder distributions. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now The bank is Canara Bank. Canara Bank Share Price Canara Bank Dividend Track Record: Why Profit Growth Outpaced Payouts Canara Bank paid a per-share dividend of ₹4.20 in FY26, translating into a dividend yield of 3.5% at the current price of ₹120.0. The bank declares a final dividend every June. The bank has increased the per-share payout over the last three financial years, from ₹3.22 in FY24 to ₹4.2 in FY26. Canara Bank split its ₹10 face-value shares into five ₹2 shares each in May 2024. Thus, for better comparison, we have adjusted the post-split dividends to the pre-split basis. On this basis, the dividend per share increased from ₹16.10 in FY24 to ₹20 in FY25 and ₹21 in FY26. This indicates a continued rise in the bank's dividend per share. Historical Comeback: Rebuilding Shareholder Payouts After the Bad Loan Cycle Like the broader PSU Banks, Canara Bank also resumed dividend payments in FY22 after a four-year gap, following a period marked by high NPAs, elevated credit costs and losses. Given the credit growth in the Indian economy and strong asset quality, the bank has reported strong profitability growth. Core Operations: NII Inches Up 0.37% as Margin Contracts 29 bps to 2.51% This growth allowed Canara Bank to pay dividends. In FY26, the bank's total business reached ₹28,06,226 crore, an increase of 12.11% year-on-year. Global deposits grew 9.7% to ₹15,68,678 crore, while global advances grew 15.3% to ₹12,37,548 crore. Because loan growth moved faster than deposit growth, the Credit-Deposit ratio rose to 78.89%, up from 75.07% in FY25. The domestic CASA ratio ended the year FY26 at 29.84%. Total income rose 7.73% year-on-year to ₹1,53,204 crore. Net interest income increased by 0.37% to ₹37,210 crore. Meanwhile, the Net Interest Margin (NIM) decreased to 2.51% from 2.80% in the previous year. NIM fell partially due to a fall in yield on advances. Financials at a Glance Source: Q4FY26 Investor Presentation Over 53% of the bank's loan book is repo-rate linked. As rate cuts transmitted across the portfolio, the yield on advances declined by 54 bps from 8.83% in FY25 to 8.29% in FY26. Further, Canara Bank’s Cost-to-Income ratio rose by 118 bps to 48.45% in FY26 as operating expenses increased. ALSO READMotilal Oswal Mid Cap Fund vs Invesco India Mid Cap Fund: Which is Better? Despite higher expenses, net profit grew by 12.7% to a record ₹19,187 crore. This profitability is key to dividend payout as the Reserve Bank of India guidelines stipulate that dividends must be paid out of current-year net profits. In addition to net earnings, dividend payouts depend directly on asset quality, capital adequacy metrics, and regulatory requirements. Asset Quality Guardrails: Low NPAs Anchor Sustainable Cash Flows As of FY26, Retail, Agriculture, and MSME (RAM) financing expanded to ₹7,30,520 crore, accounting for 59.0% of the domestic loan portfolio. Corporate loans and other advances made up the remaining 41.0%. This mix improved from FY25, when RAM advances held a 58.0% share. Balance Sheet Health: Why PCR at 94.21% Insulates Future Earnings The bank's Gross Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) reached a multi-year low of 1.84% in FY26 (down from 2.94% in FY25), while Net NPAs improved to 0.43% (down from 0.70%). Cash recoveries, tightly contained slippages, disciplined write-offs, and strong portfolio underwriting strengthened asset quality. Strengthening Asset Quality Source: Q4FY26 Investor Presentation This Net NPA ratio is comfortably below the regulatory limit required for dividend declarations. The annual slippage ratio remained well-contained at 0.24% (with total slippages limited to ₹7,030 crore). This highlights disciplined underwriting and fewer additions to non-performing loans. Asset Quality Cushion: High Provisioning Defends Future Balance Sheets A high Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR) of 94.21% (up 151 bps year-on-year) provides a robust buffer against future asset impairment losses (if any). As asset quality strengthened, the annualised credit cost fell by 13 bps to 0.59% in FY26. docs.title: 2 Electrolyser stocks in India’s Rs 19,744-cr green hydrogen race—Who has the edge?
docs.text: Green hydrogen, produced by splitting water through electrolysis using renewable electricity, is emerging as a potential industrial fuel for fertiliser, oil refining, steelmaking and shipping. According to Grand View Research, the global green hydrogen market is estimated at US$1.7 billion in 2026, up from US$1.1 billion in 2025, and is projected to reach US$11.7 billion by 2033, implying a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 32.2%. India’s opportunity is driven by its National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved with an outlay of ₹19,744 crore, including ₹17,490 crore for incentives covering electrolyser manufacturing and hydrogen production. The mission targets 5 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of green hydrogen production by 2030, supported by approximately 125 gigawatts (GW) of additional renewable energy capacity and more than ₹8 lakh crore in expected investment. By March 2026, the government had awarded 3 GW per annum of electrolyser manufacturing capacity to 15 companies and 8.62 MTPA of green hydrogen production capacity to 18 companies. However, only around 8,000 TPA of production capacity had been commissioned by February 2026. This gap between planned capacity and operating projects raises a crucial question for manufacturers such as L&T and Thermax: which electrolyser factories can secure real demand before capital costs mount? FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now #1 Larsen & Toubro: Can India’s Engineering Giant Turn Electrolysers Into a Profitable Business? Larsen & Toubro (L&T) is an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company with businesses spanning infrastructure, energy, manufacturing, defence and technology. Its green energy operations combine electrolyser manufacturing with the development and execution of hydrogen and derivative projects. Through L&T Electrolysers Limited, it manufactures high-pressure alkaline electrolysers at Hazira, Gujarat, while L&T Energy GreenTech develops green hydrogen projects. This combination gives L&T two potential revenue streams: supplying equipment and engineering systems, and developing projects that produce and sell hydrogen. Hazira’s Manufacturing Edge Needs Commercial Proof L&T’s Hazira facility is India’s first giga-scale expandable high-pressure alkaline electrolyser manufacturing facility. The company has indigenised more than 85% of its electrolyser supply chain and developed a 4 MW electrolyser stack using zero-gap technology. Its in-house research and development and testing facilities support further product development. These given capabilities can improve supply security and lower reliance on imported components. However, localisation alone does not establish cost competitiveness. Readers still need evidence of manufacturing utilisation, equipment deliveries, realised selling prices, warranty costs and margins. L&T has not separately disclosed electrolyser revenue or manufacturing profitability in its financial reporting. Panipat Provides a Demand Anchor, but Project Returns Remain Unclear L&T Energy GreenTech has secured a project with Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) to supply 10,000 tonnes of green hydrogen annually to the Panipat refinery for 25 years. The project uses alkaline electrolysers manufactured at Hazira. L&T has also commissioned a 1 MW green hydrogen plant for Deendayal Port Authority at Kandla, Gujarat. The commercial distinction between equipment supply and hydrogen production is crucial. Equipment sales can generate revenue as products are delivered, whereas a build-own-operate project requires capital investment before recurring hydrogen sales begin. Its financial performance depends on construction costs, financing, renewable electricity prices, operating efficiency, maintenance and the agreed selling price of hydrogen. The government’s own hydrogen procurement data illustrates the cost challenge. Competitive bidding under the National Green Hydrogen Mission discovered prices of ₹397 per kilogram, including goods and services tax (GST), for supply to IOCL’s refinery and ₹387 per kilogram for refineries operated by Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited. These are procurement prices, not evidence of L&T’s realised selling price or project margin. The Manufacturing Segment Cannot Stand in for Hydrogen Earnings L&T’s Manufacturing & Products segment reported revenue of ₹4,648 crore in Q1FY27, up 8.7% year-on-year from ₹4,276 crore in Q1FY26. Segment profit declined to ₹593 crore from ₹646 crore. The segment includes precision engineering, heavy engineering, defence electronics and other businesses, so neither its revenue nor its profit can be attributed solely to electrolysers. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 6.7% year-on-year to ₹67,942 crore in Q1FY27, while consolidated profit after tax (PAT), including joint ventures and associates, increased 15.5% to ₹4,988 crore. Both figures declined sequentially from Q4FY26. Operating cash flow, excluding Financial Services, stood at ₹4,300 crore during the quarter, against group collections of ₹65,800 crore on the same exclusion basis. The consolidated debt-equity ratio was 1.01 at June 2026, or 1.12 including borrowings classified as held for sale. These figures demonstrate the scale of L&T’s wider operations and provide context for its funding capacity. But because L&T does not publish separate financials for its electrolyser business, it does not show how much capital the hydrogen business requires or whether it generates positive cash flow. Does the Valuation Allow Room for Execution Risk? Source: Screener.in; Stock Price as on 8th October 2026 L&T’s share price declined approximately 6% over six months and 1% over one year. Its price-to-earnings (PE) ratio stood at 28.9. On 7 October 2026, Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintained a Buy rating with a target price of ₹4,400.

docs.title: Rs 22 lakh-crore global green hydrogen boom: 3 stocks eyeing India’s 5 MTPA goal
docs.text: The global green hydrogen market is projected to grow from about $12 billion in 2025 to $231 billion (₹22 lakh crore) by 2035 at a 34% CAGR. This growth reflects the expected demand for cleaner fuels across industries where reducing carbon emissions through electrification can be difficult. India is also preparing for this transition. Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM), the government aims to achieve annual green hydrogen production of 5 million tonnes (MTPA) by 2030. Meeting this target could require substantial additions to renewable power generation, electrolyser manufacturing, storage and transportation infrastructure. The NGHM also points to sectoral investments of around $89 billion. To support domestic manufacturing and production, the government has introduced the Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) programme, with an outlay of ₹17,490 crore. This includes ₹4,440 crore for electrolyser manufacturing and ₹13,050 crore for green hydrogen production. The mission also supports pilot projects, research and development, and the development of hydrogen hubs to help establish a domestic supply chain. The opportunity extends beyond companies directly producing green hydrogen. Electrolyser manufacturers and renewable energy developers could also participate in this investment cycle. This allows Waaree to integrate its growing solar cell and renewable capabilities. Green Hydrogen Pivot: Inside the ₹676-Crore Gujarat Manufacturing Push Waaree is building a one GW Electrolyser manufacturing facility. This plant is targeted for commercialisation by FY27. The facility is situated in Dungri, Gujarat. The planned capex for electrolyser (₹676 crore), inverter (₹180 crore), and transformer (₹192 crore) manufacturing totals approximately ₹1,048 crore. Incentives & Offtake: ₹954 Crore in PLI Wins Backs ₹155-Crore Order Book Waaree's strategy is to start with electrolyser manufacturing, then scale into build-own-operate hydrogen projects, and transition to downstream green derivatives production. It has secured government allocations under national incentive frameworks. The government awarded a PLI worth ₹444 crore for 300 megawatt (MW) electrolyser capacity. Waaree also received ₹510 crore for the 90,000-tonne-per-annum hydrogen production PLI. Notably, it has already secured an initial domestic order book of around ₹155 crore for its green hydrogen offerings. The initial focus would be on sectors aiming for decarbonisation, including Refineries, Fertilisers, Chemicals, Steel, speciality chemicals and Mobility. The ₹31,500-Crore Blueprint: Scaling Beyond Solar to Capture a $2T Clean Energy Shift In addition to the electrolyser facility, phase 1 of the inverter and transformer lines is already commercialised in Q1FY27. This is part of Waaree's larger ₹31,500 crore capital expenditure program under Waaree 2.0. Waaree 2.0 targets a global clean energy transition market estimated at US$ 1 trillion annually, projected to double to US$ 2 trillion by 2030. Waaree Energies Share Price #2 Advait Energy Transitions: Building Indigenous Electrolyser Technology Advait Energy Transitionspositions Green Hydrogen as a strategic pillar of its New & Renewable Energy (NRE) vertical. The company operates across the green hydrogen value chain, including electrolyser manufacturing, fuel cell integration, green hydrogen EPC, and asset ownership. ALSO READOnly 1 public charger for every 235 EVs: 2 stocks taking on India’s EV bottleneck Tech Transfer & Modular Stacks: Exclusive Indo-China Tie-Up Powers 100 MW Scaling Advait, through its partnership with Jiangsu Guofuhee, has exclusive Indian technology transfer, manufacturing, and commercialisation rights for electrolyser technology. It manufactures core electrolyser units in various sizes, ranging from small 250 Kilowatt (kW)-500 kW modules up to large 5 MW units. For large-scale industrial projects, multiple stacks are linked together like building blocks. These blocks create an integrated system of up to 100 MW in total capacity for green hydrogen and green ammonia production. Advait has also secured an allocation under the Government of India’s PLI scheme for electrolyser manufacturing. Manufacturing Milestones: Microgrid Proof-of-Concept Backs 95% Localisation Roadmap Advait commissioned a 30 MW electrolyser semi-assembly unit in Ahmedabad in March 2026. This is basically a working proof of concept prior to a large-scale expansion. Additionally, a dedicated facility for PEM fuel cells is being built to align with domestic procurement patterns. Advait commissioned India’s first green hydrogen microgrid during FY26. It integrated a 300 kW electrolyser and a 70 kW Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) fuel cell. Phase 1 of this facility is slated for commissioning in Q4FY27, with full commercialisation targeted by mid-2028. The company plans to localize 95% to align with domestic procurement mandates. In Q1FY27, Advait became the first Indian firm to conduct live testing of a 5 MW electrolyser test batch for 13+ green hydrogen players. Further, it completed a 1 MW green hydrogen generation EPC project in Bharuch. docs.title: Stocks to watch for October 12: DMart, Premier Energies, KEC Intl, Adani Green, and more
docs.text: As the earnings season for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27) picks up pace, several stocks will be in focus on Monday, October 12. Investors should keep a watch on the share prices of Avenue Supermarts, KEC International, Premier Energies, and Adani Green Energy, among others. Here is a quick look at why these stocks will be in focus on October 12. DMart The share price of Avenue Supermarts, the operator of DMart retail stores, will be in focus on Monday after it released its earnings for Q2FY27 today, October 10. The company reported an 8.5% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 742.98 crore for the quarter, compared with Rs 685 crore in the corresponding period last year. ALSO READBeyond CG Power: Murugappa’s other bet on India’s Rs 1.27 lakh cr chip push Consolidated revenue from operations and other income, reported as total revenue, rose 17.8% to Rs 19,644 crore in the quarter from Rs 16,676 crore a year earlier. Premier Energies The share price of Premier Energies will be in focus after it said that it received orders worth Rs 4,001 crore in Q2 FY27. The orders were from a mix of major power producers, module manufacturers, EPC companies and other customers. KEC International The KEC Intl share price will be in focus on Monday. The company has received new order worth Rs 1,014 crore in its India transmission and distribution business, including its first order for setting up of a 765 kilovolt transmission line in western India. SignatureGlobal (India) The SignatureGlobal (India) share price will be in focus after it announced the business updates for Q2 FY27. docs.title: Infosys plays down US green card freeze impact, says local workforce offers cushion
docs.text: Infosys has joined Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) in playing down the business impact of a US freeze on a key employment-based green card process. Both the companies highlighted their investments in local hiring that will help them not get majorly disrupted due to the US government’s latest decision. In a stock exchange filing, Infosys said it did not expect the suspension of new and pending Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) applications to have a material impact on the organisation. The company said it was prepared to engage with US authorities over the decision, which covers eight technology and IT services companies. Local hiring in focus “Infosys has invested in building a strong local workforce and technology and innovation hubs in the United States. The Company remains committed to its employees, clients, and communities across the United States and to complying with all applicable laws and regulations,” the company said in the filing. TCS has similarly said the suspension would not affect its workforce strategy or customer engagements, citing PERM applications in “single digits” over the past two years, according to the company. "Our workforce strategy in the US is anchored in hiring local talent, supported by a robust campus recruitment model. We have built a significant local workforce across 31 offices and delivery centers throughout the country," the company said in an October 9 exchange filing. It reiterated plans to recruit another 15,000 people in the country over five years. ALSO READTCS growth recovery gradual as deal wins moderate Eight firms affected The US administration’s action also covers Wipro, HCL Technologies, Cognizant, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe. Announcing the suspension, US Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling accused companies of misusing employment-visa programmes and excluding American workers from jobs. The Department of Labor will neither accept new PERM applications nor process pending ones involving the named companies. According to the department’s programme guidelines, employers generally need labour certification before submitting an immigration petition for permanent employment to US Citizenship and Immigration Services. Certification requires demonstrating that sufficiently qualified US workers are unavailable and that hiring foreign workers would not adversely affect comparable American workers’ wages or working conditions. Limited industry exposure Former HCL Technologies chief executive Vineet Nayar wrote on X that Indian IT companies accounted for fewer than 1,400 of the 1,17,849 PERM certifications issued in the US last year, less than 2%. “The direct impact may therefore be smaller than it first appears,” he wrote on X. Nasscom has also said Indian technology companies have reduced their dependence on H-1B visas and expanded local hiring, limiting the number of employees seeking permanent residency through PERM, according to PTI. ALSO READBEL, HAL, Solar eye strong Q2; Rs 1.5 lakh crore defence orders await govt nod Further disclosures possible Infosys said it would issue further disclosures, if required, under applicable regulatory standards. “We welcome the opportunity to work with the Department of Labor and related government agencies to answer any questions they may have,” the company said in its filing. Explaining the timing of its disclosure, Infosys said it had been verifying information and evaluating appropriate next steps after the US announcement. The filing did not quantify the total number of employees or applications affected by the suspension. It also identified its assessment of the business impact as a forward-looking statement, subject to risks and uncertainties, including changes in US immigration regulations. The company did not provide a timetable for resolving the suspension or restarting applications under PERM.

docs.title: Rs 4 Cr at 35, Rs 40 lakh salary, no dependants: 7 lessons from this Pune man’s wealth journey
docs.text: What if the biggest lesson from building a Rs 4 crore portfolio is not how to make more money, but how to decide when you have enough? At 35, Pune's Shubh Patil has accumulated around Rs 4 crore in assets. He has no home loan, no car loan and no EMIs. He earns around Rs 40 lakh a year working at Salesforce, invests Rs 70,000 every month through systematic investment plans, or SIPs, and wants to reach Rs 10 crore within the next five years. His plan is to leave salaried work, move to a smaller city and live on around Rs 12 lakh a year. He wants financial independence, but he also wants to keep travelling and pursuing his hobbies. On the surface, this looks like a story about a high earner who has built wealth early. But I believe there is more to learn from his journey than the size of his portfolio. His experience offers useful lessons on salary growth, spending discipline, investing, risk management and the difficult question of when to stop working. There is also a question worth examining. If Shubh already has Rs 4 crore and plans to spend Rs 12 lakh a year after retirement, does he really need Rs 10 crore before he can walk away from his job? ALSO READRs 4 lakh to Rs 40 LPA, Rs 4 Cr in assets and no EMIs: Pune man's FIRE journey His journey offers seven lessons for anyone trying to build wealth and achieve financial independence, or FIRE. 1. Your first salary matters less than the habits you build with it Shubh grew up in Satara, Maharashtra, in a family where money was handled carefully. His father was a schoolteacher and is now retired. His mother managed the household. He describes his childhood as simple and comfortable. His parents did not believe in spending money to show off. Instead, they focused on family responsibilities and saving for the future. Those lessons stayed with him when he began earning. Shubh completed his engineering in Pune in 2013. His first annual salary package was Rs 3.9 lakh. He did not have a large income or a substantial amount to invest. But he started setting aside a part of his salary from the beginning. "I understood that starting early was important. Even small savings could become useful over time," he says. This is perhaps the first lesson from his journey. You do not need to wait until your salary reaches Rs 10 lakh or Rs 20 lakh to start saving. The initial amount may be small, but the habit of keeping some money aside can become valuable as your income grows. Of course, saving a small amount alone will not turn everyone into a crorepati. The size of your income, how much you invest, the returns you earn and the time you remain invested all matter. But developing financial discipline early gives you a stronger foundation. 2. Growing your income can be as important as choosing the right investments Shubh's salary growth is one of the biggest factors behind his financial progress. His annual package increased from Rs 3.9 lakh in 2013 to Rs 12 lakh when he joined Google in 2015. In 2019, he moved to Microsoft at a package of Rs 29 lakh. He now works at Salesforce, where his package is around Rs 40 lakh. In just over a decade, his salary has increased more than tenfold. He attributes much of this progress to the opportunities he received and the decision to take up better-paying jobs. "Salary growth was one of the biggest reasons behind my financial progress. But earning more is only one part of the story. Saving and investing that money was equally important," he says. I think this is an important distinction. Many people focus heavily on finding the best mutual fund or stock that can generate higher returns. But they sometimes payless attention to the other side of the equation: how much money they can earn and invest in the first place. A higher income can help you meet essential expenses, build an emergency fund, repay expensive debt and invest more towards long-term goals. However, salary growth does not automatically create wealth. If spending rises at the same pace as income, the opportunity to build a large corpus can disappear. Shubh's experience shows why career growth and investment discipline need to work together. Not everyone will get the opportunities he did. His experience with large technology companies and stock-based compensation is not easily replicated across professions. But the broader lesson remains relevant: improving your earning capacity can strengthen your financial position, provided you use at least some of the additional income to build assets. 3. Avoid lifestyle inflation when your salary increases A higher salary can improve your life. It can also make it harder to build wealth if every pay hike leads to higher spending. Shubh's annual expenses are currently around Rs 14.4 lakh. Of this, around Rs 8.4 lakh goes towards rent, groceries and other living costs. The remaining Rs 6 lakh is spent on travel and hobbies. He does not believe that building wealth requires giving up everything he enjoys. "I think the important thing is to enjoy life while also saving for the future," he says. This is a lesson worth highlighting because personal finance advice often treats spending as the enemy of investing. But a financial plan that leaves no room for enjoyment can be difficult to sustain over decades. The important question is whether spending is growing faster than income and leaving enough money for future goals. When Shubh's salary increased, he was able to spend more on the things he enjoyed while continuing to invest. He tried not to let his regular expenses rise as quickly as his income. For someone receiving a salary hike, this offers a practical starting point. Instead of increasing every expense immediately, decide how much of the additional income should go towards investments, debt repayment and lifestyle improvements. docs.title: Jio changed telecom, Starlink faces the test
docs.text: Jio Platforms’ much-anticipated initial public offering will hit the market later this month, and the company has an interesting story to tell investors. It entered a crowded telecom market and upended its economics by shifting the focus from voice to data, changing the sector’s entire business model. The updated red herring prospectus is expected during the week. The IPO will put the spotlight on a company that has grown from a mobile connectivity disruptor into a wider digital ecosystem spanning cloud, artificial intelligence, and enterprise services. It may be a coincidence, but Elon Musk’s allegations that Indian business houses are blocking Starlink to protect their monopolies, with Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani among his apparent targets, have come just as Jio prepares to enter the public markets. However, the record of Indian telecom is not one of companies unwilling to compete. It is a story of businesses that have repeatedly adapted to competition and technological change, and of a market that has been transformed by new entrants and new business models. ALSO READModi@25: Steady agri-growth Jio’s entry demonstrated how a new player could alter an established market. Its low-cost data strategy changed consumption patterns and forced incumbents to respond, while the ensuing consolidation left the market with three major private mobile operators: Jio, Bharti Airtel, and Vodafone Idea. The reduction in the number of players has raised legitimate questions about market concentration, but competition has continued through tariff changes, differentiated offerings, and the battle to retain customers. Airtel, meanwhile, has expanded well beyond India, building a substantial presence across Africa. Indian telcos have competed with global players, taken their businesses overseas, and devised pricing and distribution models suited to local conditions. Their record hardly suggests that they would automatically shy away from a new technology or competitor. Their partnerships with global technology companies underline this point. Meta invested $5.7 billion in Jio Platforms in 2020, and has since partnered with Reliance on digital commerce and AI initiatives. In June, the two announced a collaboration involving an AI data centre in Jamnagar, Gujarat, with an initial capacity of 168 Mw. Google, in contrast, has partnered with both Jio and Airtel across digital services, cloud, and AI. It has worked with Jio on affordable devices and digital services, while its relationship with Airtel includes cloud and AI initiatives. Google is also partnering with AdaniConneX and Airtel on its proposed AI hub in Visakhapatnam. This is the context in which Musk’s claims need to be assessed. Starlink has signed distribution agreements with both Jio and Airtel, potentially giving it access to their retail networks, business customers, and infrastructure. Starlink gets an established route to market, while the Indian operators gain another connectivity service to offer, particularly in areas where terrestrial networks are difficult or expensive to deploy. These partnerships do not rule out commercial rivalry or disagreements. But they complicate the suggestion that Indian telcos are simply trying to shut Starlink out. A company can compete with another in one area and collaborate with it in another. That said, satellite communications pose regulatory and security challenges different from those of conventional mobile networks. Authorities need confidence that security directions can be enforced, unauthorised use addressed, and network operations kept within Indian law. Starlink, Jio Satellite Communications, and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb have licences but need to meet the remaining requirements before commercial operations can begin. So, they are at broadly the same stage of the process. ALSO READFifth column by Tavleen Singh: Congress party must do more than protest There is also a difference between opening a market and guaranteeing mass adoption. Satellite broadband can connect remote communities, businesses, and institutions beyond the reach of fibre or reliable mobile coverage. But it is not automatically a substitute for affordable terrestrial broadband. If indicative estimates of terminal costs around `8,000 and monthly subscriptions above `3,000 hold up when the pricing is announced, the service will remain beyond the reach of many households. So, early market is likely to be concentrated among enterprises, institutions, affluent users, and locations where conventional connectivity is unavailable or unreliable. That would make it a useful addition to the market, but not an immediate challenger to mass-market mobile services. Musk should also remember that a strong global brand does not guarantee success in India. Tesla has entered the Indian electric vehicle market, but its high prices and limited product range have so far kept sales modest. This should be a reminder that Indian consumers do not buy a name alone; price, suitability, and the value on offer matter. Starlink will face the same test. Securing regulatory approval is only the first step. It will have to find customers, offer a compelling proposition, and compete with terrestrial networks wherever those networks can deliver connectivity more economically. The irony is that Musk, while accusing Indian business houses of protecting monopolies, is seeking entry into a market where those same companies have built businesses by challenging incumbents and adapting to new technologies. Indian telcos have not shied away from competition, and there is little reason to assume they will start doing so now. Tesla has discovered that India is not a market where global prestige alone guarantees a win. Starlink may find the same. The government must ensure a fair and transparent route to entry, but Musk cannot expect the market to deliver success simply because he has arrived. In Indian telecom, as in the car market, the final verdict will come

docs.title: Angel One: Nifty's technical setup remains weak; Trent among 3 stock ideas
docs.text:
Angel One: Nifty's technical setup remains weak; Trent among 3 stock ideas
 From a technical perspective, the 22,200-22,000 zone emerges as a crucial support threshold, and any decisive breach below this range could weaken the near-term market structure further.
 Angel One: Nifty's technical setup remains weak; Trent among 3 stock ideas
 Osho Krishan Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 12 2026 | 7:22 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. 
 The benchmark indices witnessed a highly volatile trading week, characterised by sharp swings amid persistent global uncertainties, rising bond yields and crude oil prices, currency market fluctuations, and the RBI’s rate hike. These factors weighed on investor sentiment and kept the markets under pressure throughout the week. However, a notable rebound from the 52-week low during the final trading session helped the Nifty50 index to break its losing streak. Supported by the late recovery, the index managed to end the week on a positive note, gaining 0.44 percent and settling a tad above the crucial 22,500 mark.
 After eight consecutive weeks of sustained selling pressure, which dragged the benchmark index down by over 10% and pushed key technical indicators into deeply oversold territory, the bulls finally staged a recovery, bringing the prolonged losing streak to a halt.
 While the broader technical structure remains weak, with the formation of lower bottoms indicating a persistent bearish trend, the index is approaching a crucial support zone, coinciding with the lows recorded in April 2026 and April 2025. ‘Doji’ candlestick on the weekly chart 
 Additionally, the formation of a ‘Doji’ candlestick on the weekly chart offers a glimmer of hope for a potential relief rally. However, the overall market outlook remains cautious, with a decisive breakout above the previous swing high still required to signal a meaningful trend reversal.

 From a technical perspective, the 22,200-22,000 zone emerges as a crucial support threshold, and any decisive breach below this range could weaken the near-term market structure further, potentially accelerating selling pressure towards the 21,750-21,700 levels.
 On the upside, the immediate resistance is placed around 22,750-22,800, followed by the psychological 23000 mark. A sustained move above these resistance zones would be essential to provide near-term relief and revive buying momentum.
 Until the index establishes a convincing recovery above these levels, a cautious approach backed by disciplined risk management remains prudent. Meanwhile, market participants should maintain a stock-specific focus amid the ongoing quarterly earnings season, carefully assessing corporate performance and earnings outlook while closely monitoring evolving global developments. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 
 Stock recommendations by Osho Krishan, chief manager - technical & derivative research, Angel One 
 Stock: Persistent Systems 
 View: Bullish 
 Last Close: ₹5,770 
 Persistent Systems has witnessed a strong rebound from its 200-DSMA, coinciding with a breakout above the neckline and sustaining its upward momentum. The counter has demonstrated relative outperformance within its sector, reflecting underlying strength. The recent resurgence further reinforces the positive technical outlook, with the stock trading above all its key EMAs and the 200-day SMA, indicating a constructive bullish bias.
 Hence, we recommend to Buy Persistent Systems around ₹5,700 | Stop loss: ₹5,300 | Target: ₹6,300-6,400 
 Stock: Physicswallah Ltd 
 View: Bullish 
 Last Close: ₹143 
 Physicswallah has staged a sharp rebound from its recent 200-day SMA, forming a V-shaped recovery on the daily chart. Further strengthening the bullish outlook, the MACD histogram has registered a trendline breakout above the zero line, signalling improving momentum. Collectively, the majority of technical indicators remain aligned positively, reinforcing the prevailing bullish undertone and supporting the potential continuation of the stock’s upward trajectory.
 Hence, we recommend to Buy Physicswallah around ₹138-135 | Stop loss: ₹125 | Target: ₹160
 Stock: Trent 
 View: Bullish 
 Last Close: ₹2,920 
 Trent witnessed a strong upmove over the previous week, backed by robust volumes, effectively negating its recent corrective phase. On the weekly chart, the counter has formed a higher high, signalling a potential reversal of the prevailing bearish trend, while the latest surge has established a higher bottom. Additionally, the 20-day EMA has crossed above the 200-day SMA, reinforcing the improving technical structure and strengthening the bullish outlook.
 Hence, we recommend to Buy Trent around ₹2,900 | Stop loss: ₹2,700 | Target: ₹3,200-3,250

The possibility of further interest-rate hikes by the Fed and the RBI in the coming quarters remains a key concern for equity markets. Additionally, the upward bias in US 10-year Treasury yields could continue to influence global risk appetite and foreign institutional investor (FII) flows into emerging markets, including India. Ganesh Dongre, AVP — Equity Research at Anand Rathi, believes the Nifty 50 index faced strong resistance in the 24,500–24,600 zone last month, which also coincided with the broader 200-day EMA resistance area. A decisive, sustained breakout above 56,500 would strengthen the near-term technical structure and could signal a recovery towards higher levels. “Overall, both the Nifty and Bank Nifty remain in a cautious technical phase despite the recent weekly recovery.  Shares of Suzlon Energy Ltd. , which are currently trading near their 52-week low levels, could rise another 73% from current levels, brokerage firm Motilal Oswal projected in its note on Monday, October 12.
Motilal Oswal maintained its "buy" recommendation on Suzlon with a price target of ₹65 in its note. It highlighted five important reasons why the stock could see such significant upside: 
 Suzlon Energy's share price has corrected 31% over the last three months and is currently trading at 17.5 times its estimated financial year 2028 Earnings Per Share (EPS), which is a 20% discount to its one-year forward mean and one standard deviation below its historic multiple of 22 times.
Motilal Oswal called the valuations after the recent correction "attractive" and amidst improving earnings visibility.
"Given the seasonal nature of earnings with the second half contributing 60% to 65% of the company's annualized Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA), we expect earnings momentum to strengthen in the second half of financial year 2027 as deliveries may rise to 2.1 GW from 1.2 GW in the first half," Motilal Oswal wrote in its note. 
 At the end of the June quarter, Suzlon Energy's order book stood at 5.9 GW, providing 100% visibility on Motilal Oswal's delivery estimates until the third quarter of financial year 2028.
The brokerage expects Suzlon Energy's EBITDA to grow at a Compounded Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 22% over financial year 2026-2028. 
 India added 3 GW of wind capacity in the first half of the current financial year, according to Motilal Oswal, who also said that historically, as the second half installations have been 1.5x of those in H1, the implies addition of nearly 4.5 GW in the second half would take the FY27 additions to nearly 7.5 GW, which is in-line with the Ministry of New & Renewable Energy's expectation of 7.5 GW to 8 GW. 
 Rising power demand, mainly during evening peak hours, should support greater deployment of wind capacity through wind-solar hybrid and FDRE projects, Motilal Oswal said.
"We believe strong merchant power prices in late evening reinforce the economic case for wind capacity," the brokerage said. 
 Motilal Oswal wrote in its note that Suzlon's DevCo model has gained strong traction with orders worth over 600 MW booked within four months of the financial year and accounts for 60% of the total orders.
Internationally, Suzlon is also evaluating export opportunities in Europe, Australia, Latin America and Southeast Asia, with Australia and Europe emerging as promising markets, the brokerage noted.
Additionally, repowering in India presents a potential opportunity of up to 25 GW, given that a major portion of the existing wind fleet was commissioned between 10-20 years prior and Suzlon is expecting to secure confirmed repowering orders by the end of the current financial year, with opportunities scaling up in the next two to three years.
Suzlon Energy stands to benefit from regulatory tailwinds mandating local content, a robust providing strong revenue visibility and execution improvements through proactive land acquisitions and EPC expansion initiatives, Motilal Oswal wrote.
12 analysts have coverage on Suzlon Energy, of which 10 have a "buy" rating, and two others have a "hold". No analyst tracking the stock has a "sell" recommendation. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 67% from current levels.
Shares of Suzlon Energy ended 3.2% higher on Friday, snapping a two-day losing streak at ₹37.6. The stock is down 28% so far this year.

docs.title: Buy Piramal Finance Ltd for the Target Rs 2,480 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Growth in the kitty; profitability is next 
* Growth engine firing; multiple avenues support ~25% AUM CAGR: Piramal Finance has moved decisively beyond its balance-sheet transition phase. Growth AUM now accounts for ~98% of the portfolio, while retail contributes ~85% of AUM, leaving the legacy book at less than 2%. With retail disbursements rising ~44% YoY to INR125b in 1QFY27 and consolidated AUM rising ~25% YoY, visibility on the company’s ~25% FY27 AUM growth target remains strong. Importantly, growth is becoming more diversified. The established housing and LAP franchise is being complemented by gold loans, MFI, micro-LAP, unsecured lending and deeper cross-sell to its ~6m customer base. Cross-sell already contributes ~28-29% of business volumes, creating an opportunity to grow the franchise with lower customer-acquisition costs and potentially better credit outcomes.
* The next earnings lever will be richer portfolio mix and lower cost of funds: We see increasing scope for margin expansion as incremental originations are skewed toward higher-yielding, shorter-tenure businesses. Gold loans, MFI, micro-LAP and unsecured lending carry higher disbursement yields than the existing portfolio, and as these books season, the richer origination mix should progressively lift portfolio yields. At the same time, Piramal's improving credit ratings and greater access to diversified and multilateral funding should support a gradual reduction in cost of borrowings. Thus, we believe the next leg of NIM expansion is increasingly structural rather than purely rate-cycle driven. We estimate NIM at ~5.4%/5.9% in FY27E/FY28E.
* Operating leverage is emerging as the biggest profitability catalyst: The strongest change in the earnings profile is the widening gap between business growth and cost growth. In 1QFY27, AUM grew ~25% YoY, while opex increased only ~10%, driving the cost-to-income ratio down sharply to ~52.5% from 65.6% a year earlier. The Opex/AUM ratio has dipped consistently over the past eight quarters to 3.5% from 4.9%, despite the resumption of branch expansion. Technology and AI should further reinforce this operating leverage by allowing Piramal to scale underwriting, collections and operations without a commensurate increase in costs. Management expects opex/AUM to dip another ~40- 50bp over the next 4-5 quarters and is targeting ~2.5% RoAUM by 4QFY27.
* From growth to earnings – Piramal Finance is transitioning from the hard-work phase to the payoff phase: With the legacy book largely behind it, we believe the company has reached an important inflection point. We expect the convergence of ~25% AUM CAGR, improving NIMs, operating leverage and controlled credit costs to drive a sharp earnings recovery. We estimate PAT CAGR of ~55% over FY26-28E, with RoA/RoE improving to 2.8%/11.4% by FY28E.
* The ~INR38.5b primary equity infusion further strengthens the capital base, providing greater flexibility to pursue disciplined growth while maintaining a prudent risk profile. The stock currently trades at ~1.3x FY28E P/BV. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR2,480, based on our Mar'28E SoTP valuation.
 Higher-yielding businesses will change the portfolio economics 
* The shift in portfolio mix will be an important enabler because the newer businesses carry materially higher yields than the housing finance franchise.
* As of 1QFY27, housing loans accounted for ~36% of retail AUM and LAP accounted for ~31%, but the contribution from used-car loans, salaried personal loans, unsecured business loans, digital loans and micro-loans is steadily rising.
* The economics of the newer businesses are attractive. Disbursement yields stood at ~15.5% for used-car loans, ~16.6% for salaried personal loans and ~18.8% for unsecured business loans vs. ~11.7% for housing loans and ~12.8% for LAP.
* Gold loans could become another meaningful growth vector. Piramal Finance expanded its gold-loan branch network to 67 by Jun'26 from 22 in Mar'26 and is targeting ~200 branches by FY27-end. The business is focused on personal-use borrowers in Tier-2/3 markets, with no exposure to jewelers, bullion dealers, pawnbrokers, or wholesale customers.
 NIM expansion is fundamental, not just a rate-cycle story 
Piramal Finance's NIM was ~6.5% in 1Q, up ~47bp YoY, while the cost of borrowings stood at ~8.8%. We believe the next leg of margin expansion can come from two selfhelp levers – a richer asset mix and lower borrowing costs. The higher-yielding businesses are already generating disbursement yields well above the existing portfolio yield. As these books scale and season, we expect the higher yields to progressively flow through to portfolio yields. Meanwhile, upgrade to the AA+ rating and greater access to multilateral funding should help lower refinancing costs. We estimate NIM to improve to ~5.4% in FY27E and ~5.9% in FY28E (vs. 4.7% in FY26).
* Piramal Finance is entering a phase where the benefits of its multi-year transformation can increasingly translate into earnings. With the legacy book largely behind it, a scalable retail franchise, a richer business mix, lower funding costs, improving operating leverage and disciplined credit outcomes provide a stronger foundation for sustained profitability improvement.
* The ~INR38.5b capital infusion further strengthens its balance sheet flexibility to fund growth while maintaining a prudent capital buffer. With Piramal Finance targeting ~2.5% RoAUM by 4QFY27 and >3% over the longer term, the improving operating architecture provides a credible pathway to sustained earnings expansion.
* We model a total AUM CAGR of ~25% and PAT CAGR of ~55% over FY26- FY28E, with RoA/RoE reaching 2.8%/11% by FY28E. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR 2,480 (based on our Mar’28E SoTP).

docs.title: Poonawalla Fincorp shares down 15% in a year, will strong Q2 results boost the stock? Buy, sell or hold ? Experts' views
docs.text:
Poonawalla Fincorp reported a nearly five-fold year-on-year jump in consolidated profit for Q2 FY27, supported by higher interest income, strong assets under management (AUM) growth and improving asset quality. While Motilal Oswal Financial Services reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating with a target price of ₹ 570, Emkay Global Financial Services maintained a ‘Reduce’ rating with a target of ₹ 410.
The NBFC's consolidated profit surged to ₹ 375 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹ 74 crore in the year-ago quarter. Total income increased to ₹ 2,625 crore from ₹ 1,543 crore, while interest income rose to ₹ 2,416 crore from ₹ 1,402 crore over the same period.
Poonawalla Fincorp's assets under management stood at ₹ 74,008 crore as of 30 September 2026. Its capital adequacy ratio was 18.68%, comfortably above the regulatory requirement of 15%, providing headroom to support future growth.
Despite the strong quarterly performance, the stock has struggled over the longer term. Poonawalla Fincorp shares closed 2.25% higher at ₹ 448.05 apiece on the BSE on Friday, but remained down 15.61% over the past year.
The September-quarter performance was supported by expanding margins, lower credit costs and strong AUM growth, according to brokerage reports from Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Emkay Global Financial Services.
Motilal Oswal said Poonawalla Fincorp's Q2 FY27 profit after tax stood at around ₹ 375 crore, broadly in line with its estimates. Net interest income rose approximately 81% year-on-year to ₹ 1,380 crore, while other income increased around 49% to ₹ 210 crore.
The brokerage highlighted a roughly 25-basis-point sequential expansion in calculated net interest margin (NIM) and a reduction in credit costs to around 2.15%, from 2.35% in the previous quarter. Pre-provision operating profit grew approximately 127% year-on-year to ₹ 880 crore.
Asset quality also improved, with the company reporting gross non-performing assets (GNPA) of 1.20% and net non-performing assets (NNPA) of 0.61%, according to Emkay Global. Six-month-on-book 30-plus-day delinquencies declined to 0.35%, excluding the gold loan portfolio, from 0.67% in Q1 FY27.
Total AUM grew 55.1% year-on-year to around ₹ 74,000 crore, with new products contributing approximately 28% of Q2 disbursements. The company is targeting medium-term AUM growth of 35–40% annually, driven by new businesses, distribution expansion and deeper digital cross-selling.
Motilal Oswal Financial Services reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on Poonawalla Fincorp, with a target price of ₹ 570, implying an upside of around 27% from the brokerage's cited market price of ₹ 447.
The brokerage expects profitability to improve as higher lending yields, a favourable product mix and lower credit costs support earnings growth. It also sees operating leverage improving over the next two years as the company begins to benefit from investments in branches, collections and technology.
Management has indicated that incremental disbursement yields are around 200 basis points higher than the existing portfolio yield, which could support margins. The brokerage also highlighted the company's investments in artificial intelligence, with 84 enterprise AI projects in operation, aimed at improving productivity and reducing acquisition costs.
Motilal Oswal raised its FY27 and FY28 earnings-per-share estimates by around 3% each, factoring in stronger-than-expected margin expansion. It models AUM growth of around 44% annually over FY26–FY28 and expects a return on assets of 2.4% and return on equity of approximately 17% in FY28.
The stock trades at around 2.3 times its estimated FY28 price-to-book value, according to the brokerage. Motilal Oswal values the company at 2.7 times its estimated September 2028 per-share book value to arrive at its ₹ 570 target.
Emkay Global Financial Services, however, maintained its ‘Reduce’ rating on Poonawalla Fincorp, with a September 2027 target price of ₹ 410, implying downside from the stock's recent trading level.
The brokerage acknowledged the company's strong growth, noting that AUM had reached around ₹ 74,000 crore, up approximately 55% year-on-year. Profit after tax increased around 22% sequentially, while return on assets improved to 2.18% from 1.98% in Q1 FY27.
Emkay also highlighted improving asset quality, with GNPA declining 17 basis points sequentially to 1.20%. Credit costs eased to around 2.19%, supported by collection efficiency of approximately 99.5% and contained slippages. Net interest margin plus fees improved 16 basis points sequentially to 9.26%.
However, operating expenses relative to AUM edged up to 4.15%, reflecting continued investments in technology, collections and branch infrastructure. While management expects productivity gains and operating leverage to support profitability over time, Emkay retained a cautious stance on the stock's valuation.
The brokerage expects profitability to improve through stronger lending spreads and higher disbursement yields. It also noted that potential caps on insurance commissions under proposed regulations could be absorbed through core lending spreads and cross-selling opportunities.
Emkay marginally raised its FY27–FY29 earnings estimates by 1–2%, but retained its ‘Reduce’ rating and ₹ 410 target price, based on 1.8 times estimated FY28 price-to-book value.
The contrasting brokerage views underline the key question facing investors: whether Poonawalla Fincorp's strong growth and improving asset quality can translate into sustained returns for shareholders.
Motilal Oswal is more optimistic about the company's ability to expand margins, lower credit costs and benefit from operating leverage. Emkay, meanwhile, acknowledges the operational improvement but remains cautious about the stock's valuation.
Going forward, investors will need to track AUM growth, lending yields, credit costs, asset quality and the pace at which technology and branch investments translate into operating efficiencies.

Management has guided for 15–20% revenue CAGR over the next 3–4 years, supported by continued clinic expansion, higher utilisation, brownfield acquisitions and selective international growth. Backed by disciplined capital allocation, strong operating leverage and healthy cash generation, NEPHROPL is expected to improve ROCE, strengthen market leadership and deliver sustainable long-term value-creation
Entering into a Powerful Operating Leverage Cycle with Accelerating Profitability: NEPHROPL is well-positioned to deliver a sustained margin expansion as its network scales up and operating leverage strengthens. Management anticipates recently added clinics to mature, utilisation to improve and international operations to contribute a larger share of revenue, enhancing profitability through better fixed-cost absorption. Guided by a 15–20% revenue CAGR over the next 3–4 years (we are expecting ~21% CAGR over FY26–29E), the company is expected to convert revenue growth into faster EBITDA, PAT and free cash flow growth. Higher utilisation, rising dialysis volumes and a growing international mix will drive revenue per treatment and margin expansion. Disciplined capital allocation, selective acquisitions and technology-led efficiencies are expected to strengthen ROCE, cash-generation and long-term shareholder value.
Investment View: We expect Revenue/EBITDA/PAT to expand at a CAGR of 21.2%/20.6%/41.9% over FY26–29E. The growth will be driven by leadership in India’s dialysis market with resilient recurring revenues, an asset-light model and a strong operating leverage. Its expanding international footprint provides an additional growth engine, with rising overseas contribution supporting revenue growth and improving ROCE. Thus, we initiate coverage on NEPHROPL with a ‘BUY’ rating and a target price of INR 820, with an upside of 32.2%, by valuing the company on DCF, with an implied PE of 41x and implied PEG of 0.98x on an average of FY28–29E EPS
Optionality: Winning tender in the Saudi Arabia market is projected to significantly improve Revenue Per Patient, while accelerating growth and enhancing profitability.
Key risks: Structurally high working capital requirements, dependence on private hospital contract renewals and limited pricing power of the company.

docs.title: Buy Canara HSBC Life Insurance Ltd for the Target Rs 180 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
* In 2QFY27, Canara HSBC’s APE grew 11% YoY to INR6.6b (in line). For 1HFY27, APE grew 14% YoY.
* VNB at INR1.4b (in line) rose 20% YoY, resulting in VNB margin of 21.4% (19.7% in 2QFY26) vs. our est. of 21%. For 1HFY27, VNB grew 24% YoY with VNB margin of 21.3%.
* PAT grew 5% YoY to INR431m. EV at the end of 1HFY27 was INR76.2b, with an operating RoEV of 19.8%.
* Distribution paper is seen as net positive since CANHLIFE’s current EoM gap is comfortable vs. proposed 15%, commissions are moderate, and renewal payouts may rise. Improved affordability could further accelerate volumes, with industry-leading growth momentum to continue, as per management.
* While regulations are yet to be finalized, CANHLIFE’s current operations seem to be in line with the regulator’s directions in the consultation paper. We believe the key monitorable items are the impact on credit life due to regulations, GST drag, sub-debt-led improvement in solvency, and sustainability of the traditional mix. We have largely maintained our estimates considering the in-line performance in 2QFY27. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR180 (based on 1.7x FY28E EV).
 Favorable product mix contributes 2.6% to margin expansion 
* In 2Q, gross premium grew 12% YoY to INR25.8b, driven by 16% YoY growth in renewal premium and 12% YoY growth in first-year premium.
* APE growth of 11% YoY in 2Q was driven by 40%/66%/25%/11% growth in the Protection/Non-Par/Par segments, while Annuity/ULIP dipped 8%/1% YoY. While demand for protection and guaranteed products was affordable, ULIP was impacted by weak equity markets.
* The 23% YoY growth in traditional APE led to a rise in contribution to 55% (49% in 2QFY26), with a continued increase in contribution from protection segment and strong growth in credit life segment. Favorable product mix contributed 2.6% to margin expansion in 1HFY27.
* Apart from the product mix, favorable yield curve movements resulted in 0.8% contribution to VNB margin expansion, offset by a 2% impact due to expenses, largely related to GST-exemption.
* The channel mix, based on 2Q individual APE, was 59% from Canara Bank, 21% from HSBC Bank, 6% from other banks, and 15% from alternate channels. The recently launched agency channel witnessed an APE of INR257m in 2Q.
* Persistency ratios declined YoY in 2Q across all cohorts, except 25M and 37M persistency, with 13M persistency at 80.8% (82.0% in 2QFY26) and 61M persistency at 52.2% (58.8% in 2QFY26).
* The total expense ratio stood at 20.3% vs. 18.6% in 2QFY26. The commission ratio was largely stable YoY. While the cost ratio is above the proposed EoM threshold of 15%, the gap can be reduced in two years, aided by operating leverage and continued efficiency initiatives.
* CANHLIFE continued to deliver robust growth in 2QFY27, along with VNB margin expansion, supported by a pickup in traditional segment’s contribution, a supportive interest rate environment, and operational leverage.
* The insurer’s under-penetrated PSU bank engine, rising contribution from premiumized HSBC flows, and disciplined agency expansion serve as key growth levers. Backed by rising branch activation, product mix upgrades, and operating leverage, we expect the company to deliver 19% operating RoEV going forward.
* While the regulations are yet to be finalized, CANHLIFE’s current operations seem to be in line with the regulator’s directions in the consultation paper. Impact on credit life due to regulations, GST drag, sub-debt to improve solvency and sustainability of the traditional mix are key monitorables.
* We have largely maintained our estimates considering the in-line performance in 2QFY27. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR180 (based on 1.7x FY28E EV).
